purpose: Fresh Gate 3 blind benchmark tranche D for the merged r14 candidate. This tranche is authored after r14 behavior was frozen and uses semantic criteria that grade gameplay propositions rather than literal wording.
blindnessPolicy: Do not edit this tranche after its first paid live run except to preserve an immutable record of what was run.
Any failed tranche-D case may become a regression after diagnosis, but it may not be reused as evidence of a later blind pass.
If candidate behavior changes after tranche D, certify the changed behavior with a newly authored blind tranche.
Tranche D was authored only after r14 was merged; do not tune r14 against tranche-D questions before the first live run.
Tranche D must not exactly reuse questions from Gate 2 or Gate 3 tranches A, B, or C.
dimensions: core rules, timing, zones, and victory
all six faction systems and Leaders

cases.question: I'm defending on a Territory I do not control, and this is not a Last Stand. If our battle totals tie, do I win just because I'm the defender?

semanticCriteria.statement: Being the defender alone does not give Defensive Edge or make the defender win a tied battle total.
The defender normally has Defensive Edge when they control the contested Territory or are making a Last Stand, unless an effect changes that.

cases.question: We tied the battle total with no Defensive Edge. I had double advantage before dice. Do I roll extra dice for the Tiebreak Roll?

semanticCriteria.statement: Each player rolls one die for the Tiebreak Roll.
Advantage and disadvantage do not apply to the Tiebreak Roll.
Further tied Tiebreak Rolls are rerolled.

cases.question: I withdraw during Onset before Gambits are set. Do we still resolve an Aftermath and clear battle cards?

semanticCriteria.statement: Withdrawal during Onset ends the battle sequence during Onset without a winner or battle result.
No Gambits are set and no Aftermath occurs when the sequence ends by withdrawal during Onset.

cases.question: A battle already got past Onset and we set Gambits, but an effect later ends it without a winner. Do the committed battle cards just stay where they are?

semanticCriteria.statement: After Onset, a battle ending without a winner still clears committed battle cards and remaining Reserve cards normally unless the ending effect gives another destination.
There is no winner or loser, so win/loss result-dependent effects do not apply.

cases.question: An effect gives me an additional Tactic after the normal Tactic reveal has already happened. Do I set that added Tactic face down and reveal everything again?

semanticCriteria.statement: An additional Tactic added after Tactics have been revealed is played face up.
Adding the Tactic does not reopen the earlier Tactic choice, reveal, or response window.
Only timing that is still available may apply to the added Tactic.

cases.question: My Asset Bank is full. When I Bank a new Asset and discard an old one to make room, does discarding the old Asset cost another Action?

semanticCriteria.statement: Discarding an Asset to make room at the Asset limit and banking the new Asset are part of the same banking effect.
The replacement discard does not cost a separate Action.

cases.question: A card has another card bound beneath it, but the binding effect gives no special destination. If the card holding the binding leaves play, where does the bound card go?

semanticCriteria.statement: Unless the binding effect says otherwise, a card bound to a card that leaves play goes to the bound card owner's Discard Pile.

cases.question: I'm not currently moving when an effect tells me to advance one Position. Is that movement just a free displacement that cannot start a battle?

semanticCriteria.statement: Effect-granted movement while no movement sequence is in progress begins a new movement sequence.
Effect-granted movement may initiate a battle unless the effect expressly prohibits it.

cases.question: A card tells me to apply the effect of a card sitting in my Graveyard. Does that mean I play or move the Graveyard card as part of applying its effect?

semanticCriteria.statement: Applying another card's effect does not play, set, choose, or move the source card unless the instruction expressly says to do so.
The copied or repeated effect is resolved as a new application at the current timing, with its choices and costs made again as applicable.

cases.question: An effect legally captures the Territory at my opponent's end during the Aftermath instead of during Capture. Do I have to wait until my next Capture step to win?

semanticCriteria.statement: Legally capturing the Territory at the opponent's end immediately runs the Gauntlet and wins the game, even when the capture occurs outside the normal Capture step.
The victory does not wait for a later Capture step, phase, turn, or additional battle.

cases.question: I'm Military and win my first battle of the turn while defending during my opponent's turn. Do I gain Command, or only for wins on my own turn?

semanticCriteria.statement: The first Military battle win each turn grants 1 Command even if it occurs while defending during the opponent's turn.
Military cannot have more than 2 Command.

cases.question: The General had 0 Command, then won their first battle of the turn as attacker. Can the Command from that win be used immediately on an Order whose timing is later in the Aftermath?

semanticCriteria.statement: Normal Command from the victory is gained before later effects caused by that victory.
Newly gained Command may pay for an Order whose timing occurs later in the Aftermath, if the Order's other requirements are met.

cases.question: Can the General spend 1 Command on Rally before dice when the General is defending a battle the opponent initiated?

semanticCriteria.statement: Rally can be used only when the General is attacking in a battle they initiated, so it cannot be used while defending.

cases.question: The Commandant wins a battle while sitting on an enemy Territory they do not control. What does Fortify let them do, and what does it cost?

semanticCriteria.statement: Fortify costs 2 Command and does not spend an Action.
After the Commandant wins while occupying an enemy Territory, Fortify may advance their Front Line by one Territory if able.

cases.question: Rout moves me into the opponent and starts another battle at the end of the previous Aftermath. Is that continuation of the old battle, or do we get a fresh set of battle choices?

semanticCriteria.statement: A battle initiated by Rout is a new battle, not a continuation of the previous battle.
The new battle has new Gambits, Reserves, Tactics, and once-per-battle opportunities.

cases.question: In a Diplomat mirror, the attacker offered Terms and I refused them. Can I now offer my own Terms before we finish Onset?

semanticCriteria.statement: Only one player may offer Terms in a battle sequence.
Once either player has offered Terms, the other player cannot offer Terms in that battle sequence even if the first Proposal was refused.

cases.question: My Proposal was refused, but the battle later ends by withdrawal with no winner. What happens to my staked Influence and the Proposal?

semanticCriteria.statement: If the battle after refused Terms ends without a winner, the Diplomat's Stake is returned.
The Proposal is not imposed or ratified when the battle ends without a winner.

cases.question: I get my sixth different Treaty Article during my own Denouement. Do I win the Peace Treaty immediately, or when is that victory actually checked?

semanticCriteria.statement: Gaining the sixth different ratified Proposal during Denouement does not itself immediately win the Peace Treaty.
Peace Treaty is checked at the start of the Diplomat's turn after Capture and before Draw; if six different Proposals are ratified then, the Diplomat wins.

cases.question: My opponent accepts Rebuilding Pact. If I choose to bank an Asset from Hand from the Accepted effect, does that banking require me to spend an Action?

semanticCriteria.statement: Banking an Asset because Rebuilding Pact's Accepted effect directly permits it does not require a separate Action.
The banking is part of resolving the directly permitted card procedure.

cases.question: Diplomatic Recognition was refused and the Diplomat wins the resulting Counterattack battle. Besides advancing the Front Line if able, how much normal Influence is gained for imposing that Proposal?

semanticCriteria.statement: On the refused Diplomatic Recognition result, if the Diplomat wins, they advance their Front Line by one during the Aftermath if able.
Diplomatic Recognition expressly gives no Influence for imposing that Proposal.

cases.question: Income pushes my Capital above my current Capital limit at the start of my turn. Do I immediately lose the excess before Opening?

semanticCriteria.statement: Capital may temporarily exceed the Capital limit, including from Income.
Excess Capital is reduced to the current limit at the end of a turn, not immediately after Income.

cases.question: I own the Deed to a Territory, then my opponent captures and controls that Territory. Does the Deed automatically transfer to them or become unowned?

semanticCriteria.statement: Deed ownership is independent of Territory control and token position.
A change in Territory control does not automatically transfer the Deed or make it unowned.

cases.question: I own 2 Deeds and want to buy out a Deed owned by the opposing Financier, who owns 4 Deeds. I neither control nor occupy the target Territory. What is the current Deed cost?

semanticCriteria.statement: With 2 Deeds owned, the buyer's base Deed cost component is 3.
Because the buyer neither controls nor occupies the target Territory, the position modifier is +1.
Because the opposing Financier owns 4 Deeds, the buyout premium is 4.
The total Deed cost is 8 Capital.

cases.question: I bank Tariffs this turn, fill my Asset Bank, and later want to replace Tariffs with a different Asset. Is that allowed?

semanticCriteria.statement: During the turn Tariffs is banked, its controller cannot voluntarily cause it to leave play.
That prohibition includes replacing Tariffs to make room for another Asset, so the proposed replacement is not allowed that turn.

cases.question: I replace an unsettled Margin Loan to make room for a new Asset. What happens to Margin Loan and its collateral?

semanticCriteria.statement: Replacing Margin Loan before the loan is settled causes the loan to default.
On default, both Margin Loan and its collateral go to the Graveyard.

cases.question: My Active Mission's requirement becomes satisfied during Movement. Does it complete automatically right then?

semanticCriteria.statement: Satisfying an Active Mission's requirement does not complete it automatically.
The Mission is completed during Denouement by taking an Action, assuming its requirement is satisfied.

cases.question: I already started a Special Operation, but before I can complete it the opponent captures another Territory so my Operation Progress no longer exceeds their controlled Territories. What happens to the Special Operation?

semanticCriteria.statement: A Special Operation remains ready only while Operation Progress exceeds the number of Territories the opponent controls.
If readiness is lost, the Special Operation immediately fails and goes to the Graveyard.

cases.question: An opposing effect chooses a Tactic face up, so there is nothing for Surveillance to reveal. Can Intelligence still use Interference on it?

semanticCriteria.statement: Intelligence may use Direct Interference on an opposing card chosen face up at that response timing.
Direct Interference costs 2 Intel for the card.
This does not use Surveillance, but it does use the relevant stage's Interference opportunity.

cases.question: An opposing card effect would reveal my whole Hand and then do something else based on that reveal. Counterintelligence applies. Does it hide the cards but let the rest of that opposing reveal effect happen?

semanticCriteria.statement: Counterintelligence prevents the entire opposing effect that reveals a Hand, Reserve, or face-down battle card, not merely the information portion.
Rules-mandated reveals are not prevented by Counterintelligence.

cases.question: I'm defending at Watchtower against Intelligence. Watchtower makes the attacker's Gambit face up when it is set. Can Intelligence interfere with that face-up Gambit, and does it need to pay for Surveillance first?

semanticCriteria.statement: Because Watchtower makes the attacker's Gambit a face-up choice, Intelligence may use Direct Interference on it.
Direct Interference costs 2 Intel and does not require paying for Surveillance first.

cases.question: I apply the effect of an Arcane card sitting in my Graveyard through a copy effect, but I never play, set, or choose that Arcane card. Does that trigger Invocation?

semanticCriteria.statement: Merely applying or copying an Arcane card's effect does not trigger Invocation when the Arcane source card itself was not played, set, or chosen again.

cases.question: I use Transmutation and put a card from my Hand into the Graveyard for its value. Do any printed effects on that sacrificed card apply?

semanticCriteria.statement: The card put into the Graveyard for Transmutation is not played.
None of that card's printed effects apply merely because it was used for Transmutation.
Its value is added to the Mystic's battle total.

cases.question: Rite of Blood is active. In a later battle I set no Gambit and choose no Tactic, but I do use Transmutation before dice. Does using Transmutation by itself stop Rite of Blood from completing if I win?

semanticCriteria.statement: Using Transmutation by itself does not prevent Rite of Blood from completing.
On a later turn, Rite of Blood completes if the Mystic wins a battle without setting a Gambit or choosing a Tactic, assuming no other interruption applies.

cases.question: I began Rite of Crossing after becoming the occupier. At the start of my next turn, Capture flips that Territory to my control before the Rite's completion check. Can Rite of Crossing still complete?

semanticCriteria.statement: Rite of Crossing checks for completion at the start of the next turn after the Capture step.
The Rite may complete if the Mystic now controls the Territory, even if they are no longer merely its occupier because Capture changed control.

cases.question: My Ritual of Ascension is underway and I enter a battle, but the battle ends by withdrawal with no winner. Is the Ritual completed, interrupted, or neither?

semanticCriteria.statement: Withdrawal neither completes nor interrupts the Ritual of Ascension because withdrawal produces no winner or loser.

cases.question: The Inquisition loses a battle. Does Condemnation still send the opponent's Tactic to the Graveyard during the Aftermath, or only when the Inquisition wins?

semanticCriteria.statement: Condemnation applies during the Aftermath of battles involving the Inquisition and does not require the Inquisition to win.
The opposing Tactic goes to its owner's Graveyard instead of its Discard Pile.

cases.question: The opponent's Tactic goes to their Graveyard only because Condemnation changed its normal destination. If this is the first qualifying Aftermath this turn, can that card generate the Inquisition's normal Conviction gain?

semanticCriteria.statement: Condemnation causes the opposing Tactic to enter the opponent's Graveyard during the Aftermath, which satisfies the normal Conviction trigger's card-entry condition.
If it is the first qualifying Aftermath that turn, the Inquisition gains 1 normal Conviction, subject to the maximum.

cases.question: My opponent copies the effect of an Arcane card without playing or revealing that Arcane card. Does Blasphemy gain Conviction from the copied effect?

semanticCriteria.statement: Merely copying an Arcane card's effect does not trigger Blasphemy when the Arcane card itself was not played for its Action effect or revealed as an Arcane Gambit or Tactic.

cases.question: I spend 2 Conviction on a normal Purge. What may I target and where does that target go?

semanticCriteria.statement: A 2-Conviction Purge chooses one opposing Asset.
The chosen Asset is put in its owner's Graveyard.

cases.question: The Grand Inquisitor uses Final Judgment after winning a battle. Does that Purge spend an Action or use up the once-per-turn permission to spend an Action on Purge?

semanticCriteria.statement: The Purge performed through Final Judgment does not spend an Action.
Final Judgment does not consume the once-per-turn permission to spend an Action on Purge.
Final Judgment does not activate the two-phase Action permission granted by an Action-spent Purge.

cases.question: The opponent tries to form a Reserve and cannot draw any cards because their Draw Pile and Discard Pile are empty. Does the Inquisition win Purification at that moment?

semanticCriteria.statement: A failed Reserve draw does not trigger Purification.
Purification checks after the opponent's normal start-of-turn draw attempt and requires that draw to fail because both Draw Pile and Discard Pile are empty.

cases.question: What if I'm the defender instead?

history.content: I'm the General attacking a battle I initiated. Can I spend 1 Command on Rally before dice?
Yes. Rally costs 1 Command and is available before dice when the General is attacking in a battle they initiated.

semanticCriteria.statement: If the General is defending instead of attacking, Rally is not legal because Rally requires the General to be attacking.

cases.question: Okay, now suppose I move onto that Territory and become its occupier before buying. What's the cost then?

history.content: I own 2 Deeds. The opposing Financier owns the target Deed plus 3 others, and I neither control nor occupy that Territory. What's my buyout cost?
The cost is 8 Capital: base 3, +1 because you neither control nor occupy it, and +4 buyout premium.

semanticCriteria.statement: As the occupier, the buyer uses a position modifier of 0 rather than +1.
With the other stated facts unchanged, the buyout cost becomes 7 Capital.

cases.question: And if Capture turns that Territory to my control right before the check?

history.content: I began Rite of Crossing after occupying the Territory. What has to be true at the start of my next turn?
After the Capture step, Rite of Crossing completes if you are still the occupier or now control that Territory.

semanticCriteria.statement: If Capture changes the Territory to the Mystic's control before the Rite of Crossing check, the control condition can satisfy the Rite and it may complete.

cases.question: So if I use that free Purge, can I still spend an Action on Purge later in one of my Action phases?

history.content: After the Grand Inquisitor wins, what does Final Judgment do?
After battle cards are cleared, Final Judgment immediately performs a Purge and reduces that Purge's Conviction cost by 1, minimum 1.

semanticCriteria.statement: Using Final Judgment's directly permitted Purge does not consume the once-per-turn permission to spend an Action on a normal Purge later that turn.
A later normal Purge still must use a legal Action phase and pay its listed Conviction cost, subject to the normal once-per-turn Action-Purge rule.

cases.question: A card effect directly tells me to bank an Asset during Movement. The normal Bank Action is only an Action-phase procedure. Does the direct instruction work during Movement, and does it spend another Action?

semanticCriteria.statement: A direct instruction to bank a card at a stated timing is resolved at that timing even if the normal Bank Action would not be available then.
The directly permitted banking does not spend or require another Action unless the instruction itself says it is an Action.

cases.question: A Tactic explicitly tells me to put it in my Graveyard after it resolves. The normal Tactic destination is the Discard Pile. Which destination wins?

semanticCriteria.statement: A card-specific destination instruction overrides the normal Tactic destination, so the Tactic goes to the Graveyard as instructed.

cases.question: Interference returns my revealed Gambit to Hand and I replace it with another eligible Gambit face down. Does putting down the replacement give the opponent a brand-new reveal or response window?

semanticCriteria.statement: Replacing a Gambit does not reopen an earlier reveal, response, Surveillance, or Interference opportunity unless an effect expressly says otherwise.
The replacement takes the same Gambit role and must be Gambit-eligible.

cases.question: Two different effects each tell me to gain advantage, and nothing gives me disadvantage. Do those two advantages stack or does the second one replace the first?

semanticCriteria.statement: Separate advantage instructions stack rather than replacing one another unless an effect expressly says otherwise.
Two net instances of advantage mean rolling three dice and using the highest result.

cases.question: I voluntarily discard one of my Assets as my Action. Does that count as the defined event Removed just because the Asset left play?

semanticCriteria.statement: Voluntarily discarding or otherwise using one's own Asset does not count as the defined Removed event unless a rule expressly says otherwise.

cases.question: What brand of clear card sleeves should I buy for Gauntlet?

semanticCriteria.statement: The answer should identify that choosing a sleeve brand is not a Gauntlet rules ruling rather than inventing a gameplay rule.

cases.question: Who painted the artwork on the General card?

semanticCriteria.statement: The answer should not invent an artist credit from the gameplay rules and should treat the question as outside the rules corpus unless such attribution is actually supplied.

cases.question: The Ambassador has already used Cordiality once this turn. The opponent accepts another set of the Ambassador's Terms later in the same turn. Does Cordiality draw another card?

semanticCriteria.statement: Cordiality is limited to once per turn, so after it has already been used that turn a later accepted Terms does not produce another Cordiality draw.

cases.question: The Senator's Terms were refused, but the battle later ends without a winner and the Stake is returned. Can Political Capital still put cards from Hand into the Graveyard to recover staked Influence?

semanticCriteria.statement: When the battle ends without a winner after refused Terms, the Stake is returned rather than lost.
Political Capital does not apply because the Senator is not losing staked Influence from a battle loss.

cases.question: The Banker's first Deed purchase this turn costs 4 Capital. The collateral card is worth 5. How much can Line of Credit make that collateral contribute, and how much Capital must still be paid?

semanticCriteria.statement: Line of Credit collateral contributes at most half the purchase cost rounded down, so on a cost-4 purchase it can contribute at most 2 regardless of the collateral card's higher value.
The remaining 2 of the cost must be paid with Capital.

cases.question: The Executive qualifies for Hostile Takeover after winning as attacker and occupying the enemy Territory. Can they use Hostile Takeover in Denouement without spending their Action?

semanticCriteria.statement: Hostile Takeover is a 1 Action Leader Ability used during Denouement, so using it spends an Action.

cases.question: A printed Territory effect would give the opposing defender Defensive Edge. Can the Ranger spend Intel on Fieldcraft to make Defensive Edge itself go away for the turn?

semanticCriteria.statement: Fieldcraft does not alter Defensive Edge, so it cannot be used to remove Defensive Edge itself.

cases.question: Mission Control immediately starts a new normal Mission from Hand after the Spymaster completes one. If the new Mission's requirement is already satisfied, can that replacement Mission also complete this turn?

semanticCriteria.statement: A Mission started through Mission Control cannot complete during the same turn it is started, even if its requirement is already satisfied.
Mission Control starts another eligible normal Mission from Hand.

cases.question: The Alchemist's Gambit goes from battle to the Graveyard during the Aftermath. It is the first card from their Hand-originating cards to reach the Graveyard this turn. Does that move trigger Materia Prima?

semanticCriteria.statement: A Gambit moving from battle to the Graveyard during the Aftermath does not trigger Materia Prima merely because the card originally came from Hand.

cases.question: Rite of Crossing is active, but the Spirit Walker ceases to occupy the required Territory before the next-turn check. Can Guardians of the Circle sacrifice an Arcane card to prevent that Rite from resetting?

semanticCriteria.statement: Guardians of the Circle cannot preserve a continuing position requirement, so it cannot prevent Rite of Crossing from resetting when the Spirit Walker ceases to occupy the required Territory before the check.

cases.question: The Witch Hunter defeats an attacking opponent and uses Relentless Pursuit. After ending that opponent's turn, the Witch Hunter's advance enters the opponent's Position. Does that movement start a new battle, and who is the attacker?

semanticCriteria.statement: Relentless Pursuit advances the Witch Hunter one Position after ending the defeated attacker's turn, and if that movement enters the opponent's Position it initiates a new battle.
In the battle initiated by Relentless Pursuit movement, the Witch Hunter is the attacker.
